independent_variables.name: CEO_PAYSLICE
independent_variables.definition: CEO total compensation as a percentage of aggregate top-five executive compensation. Compensation includes salary, bonus, other annual pay, total value of restricted stock granted, Black-Scholes value of stock options granted, long-term incentive payouts, and all other total compensation. The number of executives is adjusted to five: if fewer than five are disclosed, the remaining positions are assigned compensation equal to the lowest-paid disclosed executive; if more than five are disclosed, only the top five are retained.
independent_variables.formula: CEO total compensation / adjusted aggregate total compensation of the top five executives; total compensation includes salary, bonus, other annual pay, restricted stock grant value, Black-Scholes stock-option grant value, long-term incentive payouts, and all other total compensation.

evidence.quote: The slice of the CEO’s total compensation in total top five executives’ compensation after adjusting the number of executives disclosed in proxy statements if a firm discloses more or less than five executives.

The first measure is the CEO’s percentage of aggregate top five executives’ total compensation, which includes salary, bonus, other annual pay, the total value of restricted stock granted, the Black-Scholes value of stock options granted, long-term incentive payouts, and all other total compensation (CEO_PAYSLICE).

Specifically, if fewer than five executives’ compensations are disclosed in a given year, we assume that the remaining top five undisclosed executives receive the same level of compensation as the lowest-paid executive among those disclosed in the proxy statements.
If proxy statements disclose more than five executives in a given year, we keep the compensation for the top five executives.

Our estimates are based on conditional logistic regressions because our data consist of matched pairs.

estimation_procedure.description: Conditional logistic regression on the matched manipulation/control sets. The conditional likelihood is based on the probability of being a manipulation firm given that one of the firms in each matched set is a manipulation firm. Matching is on SIC-based industry and total assets at 80–120% of the manipulation firm in the year before the manipulation period; if more than two controls are available, the two closest in assets are retained. The selected specification is the full Table 4 Panel A column (4) model for H1–H3.

evidence.quote: Our estimates are based on conditional logistic regressions because our data consist of matched pairs.
the conditional logistic regression models the probability of being a manipulation firm conditional on one of the firms in each pair being a manipulation firm

For each manipulation firm, we identify firms in ExecuComp in the same industry and with total assets in the range of 80–120 percent of the manipulation firm’s total assets in the year prior to the start of the manipulation period.
We follow Frankel et al.’s (2002) SIC-based industry classification scheme.
If there are more than two matches, we keep the two matches with closest total assets in the year immediately before the manipulation years.

preprocessing.description: Each continuous variable is winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles to mitigate outliers.

evidence.quote: Each of the continuous variables is winsorized at 1% and 99% to mitigate outliers.

scope.quote: This paper examines why CFOs become involved in material accounting manipulations.

Taken together, our findings are consistent with the explanation that CFOs are involved in material accounting manipulations because they succumb to pressure from CEOs, rather than because they seek immediate personal financial benefit from their equity incentives.
Because manipulation firms are systematically different from other firms (Dechow et al., 2011), we next estimate the following logistic regression to more formally test H1, H2 and H3:
In column (4) of Panel A we include pay-for-performance sensitivities and all the CEO power variables in the same regression.

review_notes: Selected Table 4 Panel A column (4) as the principal regression family. The paper says this conditional-logit design formally tests H1–H3, and column (4) jointly includes CFO and CEO equity sensitivities, all three CEO-power measures, and the full control block. Column (2) substitutes CFO_PPS_RATIO to address the sensitivity measures' correlation; it is an alternative specification. Panel B follows as a high/low CEO_SENSITIVITY subsample analysis of CEO-power heterogeneity. The separate H4 CFO-turnover outcome in Table 5 uses the pre-manipulation period; Table 2 reports legal-cost frequencies and Table 6 is AAER content analysis rather than regression families for the selected matched-sample design. The abstract mentions the Panel B moderation result, but the source presents it as a follow-up subgroup analysis after the principal H1–H3 specification.

Table 1 reports 116 manipulation firm-years and 219 matched-control firm-years in the compensation cohort; Table 4 Panel A column (4) reports 286 observations. The paper does not reconcile this fit-specific count with the cohort totals.
results_review_notes: Table 3 Panel A reports descriptive rows for all ten selected predictors, separated into manipulation and non-manipulation groups, with variable-specific N, mean and median. Its hypothesis-test column and Panel B correlation matrix are not treated as data-value descriptives.

Table 3 does not report a direct MANIPULATION row; the group labels and sample counts are not used to calculate an outcome mean. The source does not reconcile the 335 maximum descriptive observations with the 286 observations in selected Table 4 column (4).

Table 3 Panel A t-statistics/p-values are univariate manipulation-versus-control comparisons, not coefficient cells from the selected baseline regression; they remain excluded alongside the correlation matrix in Panel B. All ten rows’ retained N/Mean/Median values and local predictor links were source-checked.

The Table 4 likelihood-ratio Chi-square is retained as an auxiliary summary on the selected column (4) fit. Its null/comparison model and df are not supplied; no exact p-value is inferred from the marker.
